explanations: PlayerLimiter.Allow uses Reserve() and returns res.OK(). With golang.org/x/time/rate, OK() is false only when the request could never be satisfied (n greater than the burst). For n=1 and burst 5 it is always true: the reservation simply goes into token debt and reports a Delay() that this code never looks at or honours. So every request passes, and the bucket just drifts further negative. The fix is to use limiter.Allow(), or to check res.Delay() > 0, call res.Cancel() and reject.

Allow on the per-player limiter happens first and returns early on rejection, so the server-wide limiter is only charged for requests that passed the player budget. Reversing the order would let a spammer burn shared tokens with requests that are rejected anyway. Retry-After values are hard-coded and unrelated to refill rates; rate.Limiter is safe for concurrent use; Authenticate only stores the id in the context.

Sweep deletes entries whose lastSeen is older than idleTTL (10 minutes here), so the map does not grow with every player id ever seen. A recreated bucket starts full, but a full bucket of 5 tokens refills in about 2.5 seconds at one token per 500 ms, so after 10 idle minutes nothing meaningful is lost. Sweeping does not reset active buckets, does not touch sessions and has nothing to do with the server limiter.

get holds the mutex across lookup, creation and lastSeen update, so there are no duplicate buckets for the same id. It releases the mutex before Reserve is called, and rate.Limiter synchronizes internally. Go maps are not safe for concurrent writes, and get writes to the map, so the lock is needed there too.
